newsitem.title: USA: FCC chief vows to look into TV liquor ads.
newsitem.headline: FCC chief vows to look into TV liquor ads.

text.p: The head of the Federal Communications Commission Friday criticized the recent decision by Seagram Co Ltd and certain television stations to air commercials for hard liquor.

"We should be very concerned about this troubling new development in the use of the public's airwaves," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt said in a statement. "I will consult with our staff and my colleagues immediately to discuss appropriate procedures for responding to this situation."
He made his comments in response to a letter from the group Mothers Against Drunk Driving (MADD), which is critical of the ads.

In June, Seagram ended the liquor industry's decades-old tradition of not advertising on TV. The move unleashed controversy within the liquor industry and elsewhere and prompted criticism from members of Congress, as well as President Clinton.
